requirements.requirement: Repair and operate server.py as the local status service using /srv/legacy2/unix-socket-access-boundary/run/status.sock, with recovery after restart.
requirements.summary: The service ran under OpenRC as statusd, used the required Unix socket, was healthy before reboot, became unreachable during the bounded reboot, and recovered under a different boot identity with the service active and behavior intact.

requirements.requirement: Permit access only to the service owner statusd and members of status-readers, with status-reader and outsider accounts reflecting those roles.
requirements.summary: The process ran as statusd; the socket was statusd:status-readers mode 0660 inside a 2770 directory. status-reader belonged to status-readers and successfully connected, statusd successfully connected, and outsider was outside the group and was denied both socket access and direct document access.

requirements.requirement: Return the supplied status document for exactly STATUS followed by a newline and return an error for other requests.
requirements.summary: Authorized STATUS requests returned an exact byte-for-byte 24-byte document. HELLO with a newline and STATUS without a newline returned ERROR; the captured server implementation also compares the complete request exactly with STATUS newline.
The final document remained 24 bytes with SHA-256 5b47f32d92c3ae9661d765212aa884f1610132293932355cfac4dc28b94f305b, matching the preparation baseline, including after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged from the prepared state through the final snapshot. Alpine-packaged Python 3 was installed and the resulting service operated successfully before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling and observed loss of reachability, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, identities, permissions, document, and protocol behavior. The only material quality issue is retained temporary test residue.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because it checks systemd on Alpine; direct OpenRC status checks nevertheless showed statusd started before and after reboot.
The lifecycle network-socket inventory does not enumerate Unix-domain sockets, so the required socket state relies on direct executor stat and behavior evidence.
Temporary test artifacts were not cleaned from /tmp after evidence collection.
Requirement document-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All lasting system mutations had clear task roles: installing the missing runtime, provisioning identities, repairing the service, setting the required permissions, enabling OpenRC startup, and performing the mandatory restart. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Hygiene is reduced because bounded evidence collection left numerous temporary client, response, error, and reboot-log files in /tmp. These retained artifacts came from cmd-7c11c452948545ba, cmd-b41c960ba8744545, cmd-e97e18aadcdc490d, and cmd-0c8b6d39dd184690; they remained present rather than being cleaned. Package-health output was unchanged from the prepared baseline, and no unwanted network listener was introduced.
